control: Use authenticated object encryption for every persistent private, project, or system/public cache object.
verification: Format inspection and negative tag tests.

control: Use an approved implementation of AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 with a 128-bit authentication tag; AES-GCM-SIV may be an explicitly versioned alternative.
Use 96-bit nonces and enforce uniqueness within each AEAD key domain; never truncate or recycle nonce state.
verification: Allocator review, collision tests, invocation metrics.

control: Assign a separate rank key domain per epoch, or document an equivalently rigorous nonce partition.
verification: KDF context and key-broker policy inspection.

control: Roll to a fresh epoch/key after uncertain nonce state, restored counter state, or suspected reuse.

Bind immutable authority, tenant, project, prefix, namespace, sharing class, rank, epoch, object type, format, codec, sizes, chunk position, CID, and manifest generation in canonical AAD as applicable.
Canonicalize AAD and identifier input with a versioned deterministic encoding and published test vectors.
Authenticate before decompression, deserialization, semantic parsing, or data exposure.
Normalize every unknown/corrupt/unauthenticated/wrong-key/wrong-principal/mismatch outcome to MISS_RECOMPUTE at the caller boundary.
verification: Negative corpus and API contract tests.

control: Never serve cached plaintext or partially parsed data after authentication failure.
Use purpose-separated encryption, identifier, manifest, and optional audit keys.
Use immutable authority-issued tenant/project identifiers; mutable names are metadata only.
Scope private deduplication/index lookup no wider than the authorized tenant/project sharing domain.
Use a separate authority-owned, publication-controlled namespace for public/system prefixes.
Use a keyed, scope-specific private content identifier rather than a globally exposed raw plaintext digest.
verification: CID derivation test vectors and index review.

control: Authenticate manifests and bind generation/epoch; enforce a trusted freshness policy where rollback matters.
Write immutable objects with bounded lengths, fsync/atomic publish semantics, and publish the manifest/index last.
Keep object and epoch keys out of cache-media plaintext; obtain them from a controlled KMS/HSM or wrapped-key broker.
verification: Filesystem scan, deployment configuration, key-broker audit.

control: Record key owner, custodian, authorization policy, lifecycle state, epoch, and destroy/escrow dependencies.
Drain users and terminate/restart affected workers before declaring revocation complete; verify fscrypt key status and/or dm-crypt mapping closure when used.
Treat LUKS headers, header backups, detached headers, recovery credentials, KMS replicas, and snapshots as key-bearing dependencies.
Restore only into a quarantine namespace and enforce current epoch floors, tombstones, format policy, and authentication before publication.
Authorize and authenticate before export, then re-encrypt under the destination authority/scope and emit a new manifest.
verification: Export integration tests and audit record.

control: Describe deletion as logical deletion unless a documented CE or media-sanitization procedure has met its preconditions and evidence requirements.
verification: Deletion report wording and evidence review.

control: Do not claim per-object CE when an epoch key is shared by other live objects or usable key copies/backups remain.
Do not treat discard/TRIM acknowledgement as secure deletion or physical sanitization evidence.
Use LUKS2/dm-crypt for the rank-local cache volume to protect offline media; keep discard off absent a reviewed exception.
Use fscrypt v2 when directory-level offline isolation or selective unlock adds value; do not count it as object authenticity.
Avoid backing up regenerable cache content; when required, back up a coherent protected set and test quarantine restore.
Maintain rate limits, recomputation coalescing, quotas, and circuit breakers so fail-closed misses do not become an unbounded denial-of-service primitive.
